newsitem.title: USA: Cirrus Logic sees challenges, need to focus.
newsitem.headline: Cirrus Logic sees challenges, need to focus.

text.p: Cirrus Logic Inc CFO Thomas Kelly said the company faces continued challenges as in its upcoming fiscal 1998, with a key goal being to focus even more on its core businesses.
"Looking forward, we have some challenges going into FY98," Kelly said in a presentation to a Robertson Stephens conference here. "We still need to continue to drive focus into the company."
"We've got to regain some market share leadership in graphics and audio," Kelly said of Cirrus's computer chips for high-performance graphics, video and audio features.

"We need to fill our fabs consistently," he said of the semiconductor manufacturing plants, which include joint venture facilities with both International Business Machines Corp and Lucent Technologies.
"We are doing better each quarter than we did the quarter before," he said, adding that filling plant capacity was key to drive gross margins higher.
After the first nine month's of the company's 1997 fiscal year, which ends in March, Kelly said Cirrus has a "better sense of improved execution inside the company."
Cirrus is now focusing almost exclusively around Multimedia, communications and mass storage, he said.
"We have new products in virtually every market that we compete in today," he said, noting the company's sound and 2-dimensional and second-generation 3-D products.

"Shortly we'll be announcing shipping of our 56k modem," he said, adding upgraded software would be available in the company's June quarter. "We've doubled our shipments of modems each quarter. I expect that in the March quarter as well."
Shipment of the faster modems could ease some pricing pressure in the competitive market, with the new devices expected to offer opportunity for higher price points.
In its mass storage area, Kelly said "I expect that our fast storage will be the fastest growth sector, at least in the first two quarters of the next fiscal year."

Kelly declined to comment on analysts' fourth quarter estimates for the company or on expectations of improved results in fiscal 1998 after what is expected to be roughly break-even in its current fiscal year.
"My focus is on the emerging products that we are going to be delivering in June and September (quarters)," he said after the presentation.
